title: John 1:1–5 follow-up review 02 — AI-ASSISTED UNREVIEWED; NEW TRANSLATION FROM SYRIAC; NOT PUBLISHABLE
audit_policy: Append-only review of existing draft, not silent replacement or independent human review. Original five source strings and proposed target texts preserved here and in existing PR. All alternatives are proposals; none approved.

reviews.sy: ܒܪܫܝܬ ܐܝܬܘܗܝ ܗܘܐ ܡܠܬܐ ܘܗܘ ܡܠܬܐ ܐܝܬܘܗܝ ܗܘܐ ܠܘܬ ܐܠܗܐ ܘܐܠܗܐ ܐܝܬܘܗܝ ܗܘܐ ܗܘ ܡܠܬܐ ܀
reviews.prior_el: Στην αρχή υπήρχε ο Λόγος, και ο Λόγος ήταν μαζί με τον Θεό, και Θεός ήταν ο Λόγος.
reviews.prior_he: בראשית היה הדבר והדבר היה עם אלהים ואלהים היה הדבר׃
reviews.source_anchor: ܡܠܬܐ / ܠܘܬ ܐܠܗܐ / ܘܐܠܗܐ ܐܝܬܘܗܝ ܗܘܐ ܗܘ ܡܠܬܐ
reviews.assessment: mltha → capitalized Logos / definite ha-davar is an editorial lexical/title choice, not a recovery of Greek original wording. Alternatives include an ordinary word/speech term; choosing it changes connotations and needs review. The final clause must be parsed from Syriac syntax, not simply reverse-mapped from familiar Greek article rules. The unpointed ending of alha alone does not mechanically decide a/an/the or a theological metaphysics. Lwth as together-with versus toward/at requires relational/contextual review. Neither the current word order nor English tradition certifies the analysis.

reviews.sy: ܗܢܐ ܐܝܬܘܗܝ ܗܘܐ ܒܪܫܝܬ ܠܘܬ ܐܠܗܐ ܀
reviews.prior_el: Αυτός υπήρχε στην αρχή μαζί με τον Θεό.
reviews.assessment: Current Greek aftos / Hebrew hu are reasonable working back-references but weaken the overt demonstrative. Greek this one / Hebrew zeh are explicit alternatives. Do not convert Syriac grammatical agreement into proof of a particular account of personhood. Lwth decision should remain consistent with 1:1.

alternatives.note: More demonstrative, potentially awkward/register-sensitive; not a settled replacement.

reviews.sy: ܟܠ ܒܐܝܕܗ ܗܘܐ ܘܒܠܥܕܘܗܝ ܐܦܠܐ ܚܕܐ ܗܘܬ ܡܕܡ ܕܗܘܐ ܀
reviews.prior_el: Όλα ήρθαν στην ύπαρξη με το χέρι του, και χωρίς αυτόν δεν ήρθε στην ύπαρξη ούτε ένα πράγμα από όσα ήρθαν στην ύπαρξη.
reviews.prior_he: הכל נהיה בידו ובלעדיו לא נהיה דבר אחד מכל אשר נהיה׃
reviews.assessment: Current hand wording risks bodily/possession readings. Source hand-expression is retained in the audit record; an idiomatic agency rendering is an explicit alternative, not loss of a named object. Coming into existence is a contextual hwa decision; do not claim every hwa means created. The app/module verse segmentation keeps mdm dhwa at 1:3 but cannot itself settle grammatical attachment or original sentence punctuation. Existing partitive Greek apo osa / Hebrew mikol expands a relative and is not a separate source all. Compare the following life clause directly before choosing.

alternatives.note: Idiomatic agency pair; Greek loses the literal hand image. Same expression must be reviewed contextually in 1:7 and 1:10.

alternatives.scope: 1:3–4 boundary analysis, not a finished replacement verse
alternatives.note: Compare attachment of what came to be backwards to the negative clause versus forwards into the life clause. Do not move source words, change verse mapping, or invent a manuscript punctuation decision.

reviews.sy: ܒܗ ܚܝܐ ܗܘܐ ܘܚܝܐ ܐܝܬܝܗܘܢ ܢܘܗܪܐ ܕܒܢܝܢܫܐ ܀
reviews.prior_el: Σ’ αυτόν υπήρχε ζωή, και η ζωή ήταν το φως των ανθρώπων.
reviews.prior_he: בו היו חיים והחיים היו אור בני האדם׃
reviews.source_anchor: ܒܗ ܚܝܐ ܗܘܐ / ܘܚܝܐ ܐܝܬܝܗܘܢ ܢܘܗܪܐ
reviews.assessment: Current Hebrew plural agreement follows target hayyim; it is not a multiple-lives interpretation. In-him versus an instrumental reading, and its antecedent, remain review matters. Current Greek/Hebrew second clauses use past-tense copulas, but the source ithayhon construction is not itself an explicit repeated hwa. A present/current identification should be considered instead of inheriting familiar Greek past-tense wording. Absence of points/plural marks in the frozen source does not settle all analysis.

alternatives.scope: second clause only; source tense/aspect review alternative
alternatives.el: και η ζωή είναι το φως των ανθρώπων
alternatives.note: Explicit present/copying no past copula. This is an editorial alternative, not a certified source reading.

reviews.sy: ܘܗܘ ܢܘܗܪܐ ܒܚܫܘܟܐ ܡܢܗܪ ܘܚܫܘܟܐ ܠܐ ܐܕܪܟܗ ܀
reviews.prior_el: Και εκείνο το φως λάμπει μέσα στο σκοτάδι, και το σκοτάδι δεν το κυρίευσε.
reviews.prior_he: והאור ההוא מאיר בחשך והחשך לא השיגו׃
reviews.assessment: MATERIAL MISMATCH: current Greek kyrielise proposes overpowering/mastery; current Hebrew hisigo can convey reach/overtake/attain and is not a transparent matching domination rendering. Their semantic equivalence must not be claimed. The directly inspected 1903 lexicon gives the Aphʿel drk range physical/mental arrival, following/overtaking/seizing, attainment, apprehending/understanding. It does not select John 1:5 or prove victory is the contextual sense. No main alternative is promoted. Human review must choose paired semantics or explicitly retain a marked interpretive difference.

alternatives.el: και το σκοτάδι δεν το έφτασε
alternatives.rationale: Preserves a reach/overtake direction. Metaphorical reaching of light still needs contextual justification; Greek eftase can be narrower than overtook. The ancient lexical range alone does not make it best.

alternatives.el: και το σκοτάδι δεν το κατανόησε
alternatives.rationale: Paired understanding/apprehension proposal. Personifies darkness as understanding and selects a cognitive sense; possible lexical range is not proof that the passage intends it.

alternatives.el: και το σκοτάδι δεν το κυρίευσε
alternatives.rationale: Paired mastery/overcoming interpretation, preserving the original Greek direction but explicitly replacing Hebrew semantics if chosen. Victory is a contextual extrapolation, not an exclusive dictionary gloss established by this research.

reviews.lexical_support: Jessie Payne Smith (Mrs. Margoliouth), A Compendious Syriac Dictionary (Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1903), printed p.97 right column, s.v. drk, Aphʿel; Commons PDF page103 visually inspected. Own paraphrase only.
